look_here_first: First decide whether it is a woody sage: Shrubby Blue Sage is a densely branched shrub/subshrub with very small hairy serrate leaves and small blue-purple flowers.
project_tracker_diagnostic: woody densely branched shrub/subshrub; small ovate leaves with serrate/wavy margins; leaf surfaces hairy/rough; small blue to purple flowers; elongated flower clusters; dry rocky limestone/scrub habitat

project_inclusion.range_basis: Medina — UT Plant Resources Center records the Hays study plant as introduced from a cliff above the Medina River in Medina County. Uvalde — Harvard University Herbaria records E.J. Palmer specimen 11337 from Uvalde and additional Sabinal material. Val Verde — official Devils River/Dan A. Hughes landscape inventory and Laughlin AFB natural-resources inventory explicitly document Salvia ballotiflora in Val Verde County.

best_field_traits: small ovate leaves with serrate/wavy margins

comparisons.key_distinctions: Salvia greggii: Both are woody. S. ballotiflora has much smaller, inconspicuous blue-purple flowers and distinctly small hairy leaves; autumn sage usually has larger showier flowers and a different compact shrub habit.
